summary: Python TaskGroup parallel function-calls: autogenerated idempotency token collisions under high-concurrency
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports duplicate external tool invocations when making dozens of parallel function-calls from the Python SDK using asyncio TaskGroup.

Impact:
- Customer observed duplicate side-effects (two identical downstream webhook invocations) for several concurrent function-call requests.
- Occurs intermittently at high concurrency (>50 concurrent funcalls), causing duplicate billing events and user-visible duplicated actions.

Environment:
- SDK: redwood_sdk==1.8.1 (pinned)
- Runtime: Python 3.11 on AWS Fargate (platform=python:3.11-slim)
- Network: NAT + ALB, outbound through customer proxy (no header stripping observed)
- Model: gpt-redwood-open-4b, hosted (us-east)

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided minimal):
1) Install redwood_sdk==1.8.1 and run on a worker with at least 8 vCPU.
2) Use asyncio.TaskGroup to spawn 200 concurrent tasks that each call client.function_call(...) against same tool endpoint.
3) Observe tool-side logs: several invocations are duplicated (same tool payload executed twice).

Customer code snippet (redacted):
```
import asyncio
from redwood import RedwoodClient

client = RedwoodClient(api_key=...) 

async def call_tool(i):
    await client.function_call(model=\"gpt-redwood-open-4b\", tool=\"charge-ticket\", input={\"id\":i})

async def main():
    async with asyncio.TaskGroup() as tg:
        for i in range(200):
            tg.create_task(call_tool(i))

asyncio.run(main())
```

Logs attached by customer: HTTP 200 from Redwood but webhook receiver shows duplicated POST for ~3% of requests.
investigation_notes:
SRE reproduced locally with a load test harness using the same SDK version and TaskGroup pattern. We observed duplicate tool executions only when concurrency produced batches of requests that arrived at the api-gateway within the same millisecond window.

Hypothesis: The SDK autogenerates an idempotency token when none is supplied. In v1.8.1 the generator was optimized to produce a short 12-character token (uuid4 truncated + small monotonic delta) to reduce header length. Under extreme parallelism, this truncation reduces entropy and increases collision probability. The API layer deduplicates based on the idempotency token header; token collisions across distinct logical requests will be treated as retries, causing the server to replay the same funcall or route to the cached response. Since the tool system is not strictly transactional, downstream side-effects can be duplicated.

Reproduction findings:
- Reproduced at 200 concurrent tasks with 8 vCPU containers.
- Full uuid4 tokens (not truncated) eliminate collisions in repeated runs.
- Explicitly setting client-side idempotency_key per request prevents duplicates.
- No evidence of proxy header truncation in customer path; collision is local to token generator entropy.

Related code references:
- SDK commit that introduced short tokens: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/commit/3f9b2e4
- API dedupe layer: internal ticket INT-33045 (routing/dedupe docs)
comments: 2026-03-12 10:23 - Aisha Patel: Customer opened ticket. Provided initial logs and sample code. Reported duplicates at ~3% rate when running batch of 200 concurrent funcalls.
2026-03-12 15:05 - Jordan Kim: I can reproduce locally with our load harness. Observed identical idempotency tokens in colliding requests when using sdk v1.8.1. Escalating to SDK team FYI.

2026-03-13 09:47 - Miguel Santos (SDK): Confirmed generator uses truncated uuid + monotonic counter for compact header optimization. We'll prepare a patch to increase entropy fallback under parallelism and optionally expose a config flag to force full uuid.

2026-03-13 14:12 - Customer (ClipStream Media): Customer asked for recommended mitigation while we patch. They can't set per-action idempotency keys across 100s of tasks easily without changing app logic.

2026-03-14 08:30 - Jordan Kim: Temporary mitigation provided: set REDWOOD_IDEMPOTENCY_MODE=full_uuid in environment (undocumented env var implemented as hotfix in server-side SDK shim) or update to sdk-python==1.8.2rc1. Customer applied rc and confirmed duplicates dropped to 0.1% in initial tests.

2026-03-14 11:00 - SDK Lead (Priya Desai): Rolling out sdk-python 1.8.2 with full-uuid default for auto-generated idempotency tokens and a new client config option idempotency_mode: [short, full]. Patch PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/pull/742
resolution:
Workaround: Customer can explicitly supply an idempotency_key per request (recommended) or set REDWOOD_IDEMPOTENCY_MODE=full_uuid to force the older behavior.

Permanent fix: sdk-python 1.8.2 released (rolled to public) changes auto-generated token to full uuid by default and exposes idempotency_mode for backwards compatibility. Patch included tests simulating TaskGroup-level concurrency.

Follow-ups: 
- Create a short KB article for customers about idempotency token behavior and guidance for high-concurrency use cases. (Action: Jordan Kim)
- Add telemetry alerts when server-side dedupe matches exceed 0.5% for a customer in a 5-minute window. (Action: SRE)

Status: Customer accepted rc upgrade and will move to 1.8.2. Monitoring in place to verify.
